newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees strong year in core divisions.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees strong year in core divisions.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Wednesday it expects 1997 to be a "very strong year," driven by good momentum in its core businesses.

Earlier, it reported first quarter income of $0.24 a share before an $8.39 a share loss on the pending sale of its Snapple beverage operation. A year ago, it earned $0.22 a share before a $0.01 divestiture gain.
"The results of our core businesses were strong," William Smithburg, chairman, said in a statement. "We're pleased with nine percent earnings growth from ongoing businesses..."

Quaker said ready-to-eat cereal volume grew 27 percent, which outpaced the category. "At the same time, U.S. Gatorade reported 15 percent volume growth, and our U.S. hot cereals grew four percent," Smithburg said.

Worldwide foods operating income in the quarter was $78.0 million, down from $99.9 million, excluding divested businesses and a gain. The decline was due to an average 15 percent price cut on U.S. ready-to-eat cereals and greater advertising and merchandising spending.
U.S. and Canadian Foods operating income fell 22 percent to $77.2 million from $99.0 million a year ago.
Sales of $665.3 million were two percent above last yewr's $651.6 million.

Hot and ready-to-eat cerals, Golden Grain, Aunt Jemima, regional grain products and Canadian foods all had good sales gains, Quaker said. These were offset by volume and income declines in grain-based snacks and Food Service.
Overall volume was up three percent for U.S. and Canadian foods.

International food sales of $155.2 million were up three percent from $150.3 million last year, excluding the Italian products businesses sold in 1996. Operating income was $800,000, down from $900,000 last year.

"Quaker's worldwide cereal business is off to a great start in 1997," Smithburg said. "The FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration) news on the health benefits of oats was a key driver of hot cereals growth."
Gatorade worldwide sales of $284.6 million were 13 percent above last year's $251.8 million. Worldwide Gatorade operating income rose 231 percent to $34.4 million.
International Gatorade sales of $71.0 million were seven percent ahead of last year's $66.1 million, due largely to growth in Latin America, it said.
